effort: Convert a small preload or received load into a straight-ahead upper-body release.

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Receive-and-Return Chest Pass — single coach feed
explosive.job: Primary conversion of a small received load directly into forward release.
explosive.cue: Coach supplies a gentle chest-height feed. Yield briefly at elbows, then return the ball forward without an intentional pause; one feed/return per rep, followed by full reset. No surprise or hard feeds.
explosive.replacement: the Class 4 catch-set chest pass if receiving control is unreported or the first feed is not clean; if catching itself is unsuitable use a self-started chest pass and record zero catches
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-chest-pass parent; single-feed reversal variant proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First external reception-to-projection reversal with no deliberate stop, distinct from Class 4 catch-set. Continuous wall rebounds were rejected because they would hide extra catches and higher density.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Receive-and-Return Chest Pass — single coach feed

explosive.name: Two-Hand Landmine Push Press — shallow dip, feet stay planted
explosive.job: Connect a small leg preload to a forward/upward arm drive without a jump.
explosive.cue: Hold sleeve at upper chest with both hands; dip slightly, extend legs and immediately finish the press. Lower under control; no re-bend catch or bar release.
explosive.replacement: a two-hand strict landmine speed press if dip-to-arm sequencing is not controlled, or a light band chest press if the bar is too heavy
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First coordinated leg-preload-to-guided-press task. Unlike prior strict landmine pressing, the timing of force transfer is the job; it is not a lower-body power block.
explosive.key: Two-Hand Landmine Push Press — shallow dip, feet stay planted

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Shot Put Throw — controlled arm draw into forward release
explosive.job: Use a small upper-arm preload to accelerate a unilateral forward throw without trunk rotation.
explosive.cue: Face forward with feet fixed; bring the light ball slightly forward, draw it smoothly back toward the shoulder, then immediately push forward to release. No side-on wind-up.
explosive.replacement: a stationary forward-facing single-arm throw if the arm draw causes rotation or loss of ball control; use a secured single-arm band press if ball fit or containment fails
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Related to Class 1 unilateral projection; adds a controlled reversal problem, not a different stance or heavier ball. Only two releases per arm limit repeated anterior-shoulder demand.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Shot Put Throw — controlled arm draw into forward release

explosive.name: Band Lat Pulldown — controlled upward reach into fast draw
explosive.job: Link an overhead loaded reach to a quick elbow-and-shoulder pull.
explosive.cue: Use a rated overhead attachment and tall kneeling base; allow hands upward for 2 s, then reverse smoothly into a quick pull toward ribs. No torso crunch.
explosive.replacement: a paused light Band Lat Pulldown if reversal control is absent
explosive.identity: band-lat-pulldown parent; bilateral reversal delivery proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Related to Class 3 vertical elbow drive. Its role is a controlled reversal in the pulling direction, complementing the received-load press; not counted as a new pulling family.
explosive.key: Band Lat Pulldown — controlled upward reach into fast draw

explosive.name: Plyo Push-Up — two linked pairs on elevated hands
explosive.job: Practice one brief hand-contact reversal before fully resetting.
explosive.cue: Four push-offs total: perform two small hand-flight reps linked by one soft reception, rest 15 s, then two more. No clap. Use only if prior hand-flight control and first reception are satisfactory; otherwise four separate reps.
explosive.replacement: four separated elevated-hand plyo push-ups, resetting 12 s between each, when linked reception is unconfirmed; use non-flight fast presses if hand landing is unsuitable
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Introduces a single receive-to-push link rather than changing support height. Four hand landings replace Class 4's six paused-start landings; a long rebound series was rejected. With absent control evidence, separated reps are the conservative replacement.
explosive.key: Plyo Push-Up — two linked pairs on elevated hands

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Forward Throw — fixed stance, arm-driven
explosive.job: Project from a higher arm position while retaining a forward release line.
explosive.cue: Light ball, both feet fixed; bring ball to comfortable overhead position, ribs down, throw forward with both arms. No back arch, full-body whip or overhead catch.
explosive.replacement: a tall-kneeling chest pass if overhead range cannot stay comfortable, or a self-anchored band speed press if release space is unsuitable
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-overhead-throw; generated canonical family; fixed-foot arm-driven execution
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First forward overhead release, distinct from chest-height projection and downward slams. Selected for release-path coverage, not as a claim that another throw is a chest-pass comparison.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Overhead Forward Throw — fixed stance, arm-driven

resilience.name: Band Pull-Apart — low light tension
resilience.job: Lightly strengthen scapular retraction after the received-load and arm-draw tasks.
resilience.cue: Hands at comfortable chest height, elbows softly fixed; separate hands 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without shrugging or rib flare.
resilience.replacement: a smaller-range pull-apart with a lighter band
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier

resilience.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
resilience.job: Lightly load each shoulder's external-rotation control before the main pressing sets.
resilience.cue: Lie on side, top elbow at ribs near 90 degrees; very light dumbbell, rotate outward 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s without rolling back.
resilience.replacement: unanchored bilateral light-band external rotation for 1 × 6 if floor side-lying is unsuitable; record bilateral dosing
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier

primary.name: Floor Press — two dumbbells, neutral grip
primary.job: Main horizontal pressing force with a reproducible floor-limited range.
primary.cue: Lower 2 s, touch upper arms gently, pause 1 s, then press decisively; feet stay down. Coach supervises pickup/set-down.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor press through controlled comfortable range

primary.name: One-Arm Row — dumbbell, hand and knee on bench
primary.job: Load the arm-driven backward draw while support prevents torso rotation.
primary.cue: Draw elbow toward hip, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; stop before the shoulder rolls forward or the trunk turns.
primary.replacement: a thigh-supported dumbbell row with the same arm path if a bench does not fit

primary.name: Push-Up — controlled full repetition
primary.job: Load the press with free shoulder-blade movement and a steady trunk.
primary.cue: Lower 2 s, push decisively, finish tall through shoulders for 1 s; no hand flight. Adjust leverage or band resistance to reach 2–3 RIR.
primary.replacement: a hands-elevated push-up on an inspected immovable support

primary.name: Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row — bilateral, hinged
primary.job: Strengthen the wider-elbow backward draw that controls the arm-open position.
primary.cue: Hold a still hinge; elbows about 60 degrees from torso, pull to upper ribs, hold 1 s, lower 2 s.
primary.replacement: a chest-supported version only on an inspected bench with adequate arm clearance

primary.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher — floor-supported
primary.job: Load elbow extension for the finish of a forceful press.
primary.cue: Neutral grips, upper arms near vertical; lower 2 s beside the ears, extend under control without shoulder swing.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor-supported elbow extension through comfortable range

primary.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl — simultaneous arms
primary.job: Load elbow flexors for finishing the backward draw without another shoulder-extension set.
primary.cue: Upper arms stay at ribs; lift 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s, without hip swing or wrist collapse.
primary.replacement: a lighter neutral-grip curl without body movement

progression: Class 4 included six paused hand landings and three catch-set passes. This class prescribes at most four hand landings and six gentle feed-return catches, with conservative same-slot versions when the prerequisites are not demonstrated. Class 1/2 Floor Press and Row doses return at 2 × 6 and 2 × 6 per arm, while Push-Up and elbow-extension support drop to 1 × 6 each. Eight working rounds remain; pressing working cycles per arm drop from Class 4's 32 to 24 to make room for receiving/reversal exposure. No load increase is earned by the sequence. Advance only after actual smooth reception, forward line, technical reserve and satisfactory recovery.
audit_findings: Removed continuous rebound chains and reduced hand-flight and supporting pressing volume. Paired push-ups explicitly contain four push-offs/landings, not four pairs; the gap pattern is 0/15/0 seconds. Gentle feed-return is the only catch task and is counted as six catches. Three new task types and three related variants are recorded. No rotational throws, re-bend landmine catch, added jumping or fifteenth assessment.
next_job: Class 6 should consolidate with reduced overall demand and review all actual response available at the midpoint; do not assume Class 5's receiving or linked contacts were performed.
